concept.title: Symmetric-Key Cryptanalysis: Differential and Linear Cryptanalysis Bounds
concept.concept_description: Prove tight upper bounds on the differential probability of an S-box. Formalize the wide-trail strategy used in AES: prove that the minimum number of active S-boxes in 4 rounds of AES is 25. Connect to the branch number of the MixColumns matrix.

concept.title: Graph Coloring: Chromatic Polynomial Theory
concept.concept_description: Formalize chromatic polynomials and prove deletion-contraction. Prove the four-color theorem is equivalent to χ(G) ≤ 4 for all planar G. Formalize Brooks' theorem: χ(G) ≤ Δ(G) unless G is complete or an odd cycle. Prove the chromatic polynomial is T-positive for claw-free graphs.
concept.mathematical_framing: Formalize chromatic polynomials and prove deletion-contraction. Prove the four-color theorem is equivalent to χ(G) ≤ 4 for all planar G. Formalize Brooks' theorem: χ(G) ≤ Δ(G) unless G is complete or an odd cycle. Prove the chromatic polynomial is T-positive for claw-free graphs.

concept.title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography: Weil Pairing and BLS Signatures
concept.concept_description: Formalize the Weil pairing on an elliptic curve and prove its bilinearity. Show that the BLS signature scheme is existentially unforgeable under the computational Diffie-Hellman assumption in the pairing group. Prove that the pairing allows short aggregate signatures.

concept.title: Classification of Perfect Cubes in 14-gonal Numbers
concept.concept_description: The only non-negative integer solutions (n, t) to the Diophantine equation P_14(n) = t^3 are (0,0), (1,1), and (5,5), where P_s(n) = ((s-2)n^2 - (s-4)n)/2 denotes the n-th s-gonal number. This corresponds to the k=5 case of Theorem 1(ii) in the paper.
concept.mathematical_framing: The only non-negative integer solutions (n, t) to the Diophantine equation P_14(n) = t^3 are (0,0), (1,1), and (5,5), where P_s(n) = ((s-2)n^2 - (s-4)n)/2 denotes the n-th s-gonal number. This corresponds to the k=5 case of Theorem 1(ii) in the paper.
concept.lean_guess: Translate the Diophantine equation 6n^2 - 5n = t^3 into an elliptic curve problem, compute the Mordell-Weil group of the corresponding curve, and use linear forms in logarithms along with modular methods to bound and verify the finite set of integer points.
